exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS allows attackers to bypass certificate-based authentication, enabling forged or stolen certificates to impersonate clients or servers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or expired certificate validation allows attackers to exploit improperly validated certificates to intercept or spoof communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Use of deprecated TLS protocols or weak cipher suites directly corresponds to weakened encryption that attackers can exploit to decrypt traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Symmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak cipher suites in TLS sessions undermine the symmetric cryptography used to protect data in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Deploy Container
exploitedBy.relevance: Replaying captured deployment manifests can cause unauthorized container deployments, directly exploiting the deployment pipeline.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks may reuse captured tokens or credentials embedded in manifests to authenticate and execute deployments.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Bearer tokens transmitted over unprotected channels can be intercepted and stolen for unauthorized API access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Without payload signing, attackers can tamper with manifests in transit by subverting trust verification mechanisms.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of manifest signing means attackers can modify payloads without valid certificate-based integrity checks detecting the tampering.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, attackers can flood the API with deployment requests, exhausting control plane resources and causing denial of service.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud API
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can abuse cloud APIs without rate limiting to programmatically trigger excessive deployments and disrupt operations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Web Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Cleartext fallback channels allow attackers to intercept or inject data into communications using standard web protocols without encryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted fallback channels can be exploited for data exfiltration over alternative unmonitored protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS hijacking directly enables redirection of API traffic by compromising DNS infrastructure to resolve domains to attacker-controlled endpoints.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Domain Fronting
exploitedBy.relevance: BGP or DNS route hijacking can be combined with domain fronting techniques to covertly redirect and intercept API communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Digital Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Without revocation checking, attackers can use previously compromised or revoked certificates to authenticate, as installations of malicious certificates go undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container CLI/API
exploitedBy.relevance: Oversized manifest payloads submitted via container APIs can overwhelm and disrupt the control plane processing resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Embedded Payloads
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers may embed excessively large or malicious content within manifest payloads to disrupt control plane parsing and processing.
